source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-35

procedures.title: Differential carrier: remove and install
steps: (continued) Mark the camber cam and bolt positions on the strut rod bracket and loosen the cam bolts.
Remove the 4 bolts holding the bracket to the carrier underside and drop the bracket; remove the camber cam bolts and swing the strut rods up out of the way.
Remove the 8 carrier-to-cover bolts, loosening them gradually so the lubricant drains.
Pull the carrier part way out of the cover, drop its nose to clear the crossmember, and work it down and out.
Installation: clean the inside of the carrier cover, grease the gasket surface well and lay a new gasket on the cover.
Make 2 aligning studs by cutting the heads off two 1/2"-13 x 1-1/4" bolts and slotting the plain end; screw them into two carrier bolt holes below center, one each side.
Lift the carrier into place, guiding the studs into the cover (see figure 87 in the manual).
Fit the carrier-to-cover bolts and tighten securely.
Connect the propeller shaft to the companion flange and transmission yoke.
Fit the rubber cushion on the bracket, place it on the frame crossmember, fit the nut and torque to specification.
Lift the drive shafts into place and clamp the inboard trunnions to the side gear yokes with the U-bolts.
Attach the strut rods to the bracket, lift the bracket under the carrier, fit the 4 bolts and torque to specification; set the camber cams to their marks and tighten the cam nuts.
Reconnect the spring end link bolts (see Spring Installation).
Remove the filler plug on the right side of the cover and fill with hypoid lubricant up to the hole.
Lower the car and road test for leaks, noise and general operation.

procedures.title: Positraction differential: on-vehicle check
steps: With a manual transmission, put it in neutral.
Raise the rear until the wheels are clear and remove one wheel and tire.
Fit adapter J-5748 to the axle shaft flange and put a 1/2-13 bolt in the adapter (see figure 88 in the manual).
Hold the other wheel firmly so it cannot turn, and read the torque needed to turn the axle with a 0-150 lb-ft torque wrench on J-5748.
notes: Positraction is optional and fits in the standard carrier in place of the regular differential; service is the same as a standard axle apart from this check.
J-5748 is listed among the Corvette rear suspension special tools (figure 105).

procedures.title: Propeller shaft and universal joints: general description
steps: If a driveline clunk develops on a car with the 3-speed automatic, clean the slip yoke spline and pack it with about one tablespoon of lithium soap base chassis lube.
notes: All models use a one-piece, exposed tubular propeller shaft with extended-life cross-type U-joints that need no periodic maintenance.
The splined front yoke slides into the transmission output shaft, letting the shaft length change slightly as the axle moves up and down.

Two versions exist: Dana (see figure 89 in the manual) and Saginaw (see figure 90 in the manual); some applications carry a damper, which is not serviced separately; replace the sleeve and damper as an assembly (see figure 91 in the manual) to avoid imbalance.
The spline needs no periodic service; an O-ring in the transmission output shaft keeps transmission oil from reaching it.
